question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{x}, & -\sqrt{e}<x<-1 \\ \frac{1}{4}, & -1\le x<1\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{e}}^{1}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{e}}^{-1}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{e}}^{-1}x\cdot (-\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{-\sqrt{e}}^{-1}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{x}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x{|}_{-\sqrt{e}}^{-1}+{\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =1-\sqrt{e}+\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{8} \\  & =1-\sqrt{e}\end{aligned}
$$
